sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: No macro-signals series is flagged extreme heading into the week; the strongest readings are both elevated on the upside — S&P 500 (z=+1.86) and Nasdaq 100 (z=+1.85) — meaning equities are stretched versus their 3-year mean rather than showing stress. VIX sits at 14.94 (z=-0.51), squarely normal. Gold is the other elevated print (z=+1.50), a mild flight-to-quality bid running alongside the equity melt-up. The S&P 500 is up about 3.5% over the past month (7413 to 7676), grinding higher into a week headlined by large-cap tech reporters.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Five reporters from the SP500/R1000/isCore pool land Tuesday through Thursday — outside this week's strongest board-wide movers (mining +6.62%, copper +2.63%, oil-gas -2.15%) but concentrated in technology, which carries a modest +0.69% median 3-day reaction across 475 tickers. Tue: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Medtronic (MDT) open the week on cybersecurity spend and devices. Wed: Broadcom (AVGO), the week's largest name at roughly $1.7T market cap, reports into that same technology cohort. Thu: Copart (CPRT) plugs into industrials' -1.32% median reaction — the sharpest sector move touching this pool — while Lululemon (LULU) gives a consumer-cyclical (-0.51% median) read on apparel retail.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table this cycle at +6.62% median across 151 tickers on a thick 2,626-item news window, with copper close behind in the same complex at +2.63% (6 tickers, 247 items — not yet thick). Oil-gas pulls the other way at -2.15% across 33 names on a thick 1,005-item window; none of next week's SP500/R1000/isCore reporters sit inside either commodity complex, so this week's calendar tests technology and industrials instead.
